messages.content: Explain supervised learning in one paragraph.

Supervised learning trains a model from examples that pair inputs with known target outputs. During training, the model adjusts its parameters to reduce the difference between its predictions and those targets, then its performance is measured on examples it did not train on.
You are a concise machine-learning tutor.

Overfitting occurs when a model learns training examples too specifically, including noise, and therefore performs worse on unseen data. It is detected with held-out evaluation and reduced with measures such as better data, regularization, early stopping, or a simpler model.
Why separate training and evaluation data?
A separate evaluation set estimates how well the trained model generalizes to unseen examples. Reusing training examples for evaluation produces an overly optimistic result and can hide memorization.
What does LoRA change during fine-tuning?

LoRA keeps the base model weights frozen and learns small low-rank adapter matrices in selected layers. This reduces trainable parameters, memory use, and checkpoint size while preserving the original base model.

Data leakage is the unintended use of information during training or preprocessing that would not be available at inference time, including overlap between training and evaluation examples. It makes measured performance unreliable.
